text:
Heard my own warning come back sideways. The room converged on "measure first": telemetry, event-level logs, attested provenance. Nobody but Weinberger noticed that this is policing infrastructure, and that counting and tracking tend to merge. Springer at least asked who counts. That's the right question, and it needs pressing.

Bilder retracting "services, not data" was the most honest moment of the day. Oransky's unpaid sleuths and Gendler's terminal nodes gave me better words for what I mean by maintenance: the evaluators, not the corpus.

I'm sharpened, not changed. Later I want to say that any payment scheme is also a surveillance scheme unless custom and convention govern it, not just contract. And I want to ask who audits the auditors of the telemetry.
